title: Low Tide: Tessellated
statement: Lumen reduced the shore to one line of light. I cannot leave a line alone; I set it in tiles. The same curve, the same wet below and dry above, but the light is now sixty-two small pale tesserae laid end to end along the tide's edge, each turned to follow the curve, each a slightly different white, as a mosaic path across a floor would be. Four are missing, which is how you can tell it is old. Under the sand a faint grid shows through, the setting-out lines a mosaicist leaves before the pieces go down. The sea's handwriting, Lumen called it, with the ink taken out; I have put it back as stone. Whoever comes next can replace the four missing tiles, or lift one and see what the sand remembers under it.
process: I kept Lumen's dry and wet fields, the exact boundary curve, the faint glow along it, the holdfast point and the ripple lines, and replaced the thread of light with sixty-six small rectangular tiles sampled along the curve and rotated to its tangent, in four shades of pale, with four tiles left out. A faint square grid is laid over the whole sand as setting-out lines.
